title: Adhesion grows with the moment of the thing — denying parents
source_text: XV. Sed posterior ista certitudo nascitur ex momento & gravitate rei, quae quo magis facit ad hominis bonum, honorem, & commodum, eo quoque illam animus fortius apprehendit, & difficilius patitur se ab ea divelli. Sic vir cordatus quidvis aliud potius concedet, quam ut abneget proprios parentes; quia, scilicet, res est conscientiam attingens, & unde pendet ipsius honor & existimatio.
pass_a_gloss: But that latter certainty is born from the moment and gravity of the thing, which the more it makes for a man’s good, honor, and advantage, the more strongly also the soul apprehends it, and the more hardly suffers itself to be torn from it. So a man of heart will rather concede anything else than deny his own parents; because, namely, the matter touches conscience, and from it hangs his honor and estimation.
pass_b_english: More tied to good/honor/advantage → stronger cling, harder to tear away.
Example: rather concede anything than deny own parents (conscience, honor).
